name: OR-06
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by about six points on the partisan baseline
Incumbent Andrea Salinas is running with a large fundraising edge
Republican David Russ has raised only about $13,000 with $21 on hand
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 96%
model.rationale: Salinas is an incumbent in a district that leans Democratic, and the money gap is overwhelming: she has raised over $1.6 million while Russ has raised almost nothing and lacks outside support. Markets and fundamentals both point to a comfortable Democratic hold, so the forecast stays at a roughly 20-point margin.
model.watch: Any late outside spending against Salinas or a strong Republican national environment could narrow the margin, though a seat flip remains unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Oregon's 6th District is a first-term Democratic seat held by Andrea Salinas, who is running for reelection. The district leans Democratic by about six points, and the national environment adds to that advantage. No independent general-election polls are available, and no expert raters have flagged the race as competitive.

The clearest signal is financial: Salinas has raised about $1.6 million with $611,000 on hand, while Republican David Russ has raised roughly $13,000 with just $21 in the bank and no outside spending on either side. Prediction markets price a Democratic win at about 96%. The race is rated Safe D, with the main uncertainty coming from the lack of polling rather than any specific sign of a contest.
